newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude programmes point to higher Jan output.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude programmes point to higher Jan output.

text.p: North Sea crude oil output from the eight largest fields in January is set to rise 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) to an average 4.71 million bpd from 4.67 million bpd in December, according to traders who have seen the preliminary schedules.
The Ekofisk and Forties systems are mostly responsible for the rise in output, while Brent's January programme is smaller than December.
Ekofisk is due to load two million barrels more than in December, and Forties will load an extra million barrels.
Flotta, Gullfaks, Oseberg, Statfjord and Troll loadings are due to be unchanged, and Brent is expected to fall 800,000 barrels.
